title: Ambient conjugation formula for canonical completed scalar associativity
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,L,M$ be finite-dimensional extension fields of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, let $i:E\to L$ and $j:L\to M$ be $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra maps, and let $T$ be a scheme. Write $I_a,I_b,I_c$ for the completed integral scalar extensions and $L_a,L_b,L_c$ for the ordinary derived extensions along their completed coefficient-sheaf maps. On derived-complete objects write $\chi_a:L_a\simeq I_a$ for the specified completed comparison. Let $\alpha:L_bL_a\simeq L_c$ be the adjunction-normalized ordinary derived scalar associator. For every intrinsic bounded constructible integral object $K$ over $E$, the ambient image of the canonical intrinsic integral scalar associator (with the auxiliary characteristic parameter $p=0$) equals $\chi_b(I_aK)^{-1}L_b(\chi_a(K)^{-1})\alpha_K\chi_c(K)$, with compositions read from left to right. The intermediate input $I_aK$ is derived complete, so every displayed inverse is defined.

proof.text: The two ordinary tensor functors use the same specified scalar-extension witness. Expand the quotient-to-derived comparison in the compact-support cochain counit; its extra maps are identity maps, so that counit equals completedScalarCounit.

Compare the normalized completed-line sheaf associator with the ordinary scalar associator on successive tensor units. Both send one tensor one tensor x to one tensor x. The two successive scalar adjunction Hom bijections detect equality.

For a good complex P, the ordinary derived associator has the successive-counit formula proved by the preceding node. Replace its ordinary sheaf associator by the equal completed-line sheaf associator. The normalized associator-data specification is the same formula. The direct counit is invertible by the exact model, so cancel it. Extensionality of natural transformations through the good-complex localization then identifies the two derived associators.

The canonical-restriction specification identifies the intrinsic associator component with the completed-line associator. The latter is defined as conjugation of its ordinary derived associator by chi. Substitute the derived equality and obtain the formula.

theorem completedScalarCanonicalAssociatorFormula (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E T) :
    ((sfIntegralScalarComp l E L i T 0 (Fact.out : l.Prime).ne_zero M j).hom.app K).hom =
      (CompletedLineTensor.chi l L T M j _
        (CompletedLineTensor.extension_complete l E T L i K.obj
          (CompletedLineTensor.intrinsic_complete l E T K))).inv ≫
      (pbcDerivedExtend (completedCoefficientMap l L M j T)).map
        (CompletedLineTensor.chi l E T L i K.obj
          (CompletedLineTensor.intrinsic_complete l E T K)).inv ≫
      (PurCompactSupport.tensorComposition _ _ _
        (PurCompactSupport.completedMap_composition l E L i M j T)).hom.app K.obj ≫
      (CompletedLineTensor.chi l E T M (j.comp i) K.obj
        (CompletedLineTensor.intrinsic_complete l E T K)).hom
